paragraphs: Children in care in the Stirling area are looked after by Stirling Council's adoption and fostering team, shown above alongside the independent services that take enquiries from the area. The council says it needs more foster carers so that children can stay in their own communities wherever possible.

Its carers offer short-term care, from a few days to several months, for children of any age, keeping brothers and sisters together where possible; long-term care, mostly for children over eight who cannot return home; short breaks, from every weekend to once a month, including for children with significant disabilities; and enhanced care for older children with higher emotional and behavioural needs. The council also runs a Host Family Scheme for unaccompanied young people seeking asylum, many of them over 16, open to anyone in or within reach of Stirling with a spare room.

After an enquiry, a phone call and a home visit, you take the Skills to Foster course and are assessed by a supervising social worker, which the council aims to finish within six months, before a fostering panel. Checks include PVG membership for you and anyone in the household over 16, a medical through your GP, and six references, two of which can be from relatives.

Approved carers get a named supervising social worker, the council's out-of-hours emergency team, looked-after children's nurses from NHS Forth Valley and ongoing training. The council pays a weekly fee as well as an allowance for each child, 28 days' holiday on full fee, extra payments for birthdays, Christmas and the summer holidays, and mileage. Its page does not give a year for its figures, so ask for current rates. From April 2026 the Scottish Recommended Allowance, the national minimum for a child's costs, is £177.68 a week for ages 0 to 4, £206.71 for 5 to 15 and £283.35 for 16 and 17; any carer fee is paid on top.
Contact the team on 01786 404040, and see our Falkirk, Clackmannanshire and Scotland pages for nearby services.
